chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father and Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani, altogether from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Suleiman ibn Dawud al-Minqari, from Hafs ibn Ghiyath, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'All goodness is placed in a house, and its key has been made to be asceticism (zuhd) in the world.'

Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: A man will not find the sweetness of faith in his heart until he does not care about consuming the world.'
Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'It is prohibited upon your hearts that you recognize the sweetness of faith until you are ascetic in the world.'

key_terms.الزُّهْدَ: Asceticism or detachment from worldly desires

ai.seo_question: What is the key to finding the sweetness of faith according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) identifies asceticism (zuhd) as the 'key' to all goodness, linking it directly to the Prophet’s declaration that the 'sweetness of faith' remains inaccessible to hearts attached to worldly consumption. This hadith, found in al-Kafi’s chapter on condemning the world, underscores the Shia scholarly view that zuhd is not merely poverty but a spiritual detachment that purifies the heart, making the recognition of faith obligatory for those whose hearts are veiled by worldly love.
